solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing; clues and answers read from cryptics.georgeho.org (ODbL)'s copy of the post

clue.text: Girl dancing with a brat in place noted for rock

indicators.note: letters that are dancing move about, so the girl, a and brat are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl dances alongside an unruly child somewhere famous for its rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' signals an anagram of GIRL + A + BRAT. 'Rock' suggests music or sweets, but here it is the great limestone rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The British territory at the tip of Spain is dominated by the famous limestone Rock.

clue.text: Electronic publication set up for football maybe

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: an e-mag is an electronic magazine

explanation.surface: An online magazine has been launched for football fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' in a down clue reverses EMAG (e-mag, an online magazine).
explanation.definitionFit: Football is one example of a sport or game, hence the 'maybe'.

clue.text: Old boy going up unpleasant part of city?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece going up sits above the second in the column

parts.note: BO is the usual abbreviation for old boy
rough can mean unpleasant, as in a rough time

explanation.surface: A former pupil heads into a rough, seedy district of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' puts BO above ROUGH in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A borough is an administrative district, often one division of a large city such as London.

clue.text: A quiet wood

parts.note: sh is the command to be quiet

explanation.surface: A peaceful stretch of woodland.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash is a hardwood timber, the wood of the ash tree, used for tool handles.

clue.text: European getting you upset, a failure

parts.note: a Turk comes from ..., partly in Europe

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned over, so the word is read upwards

parts.note: ye is an old form of you

explanation.surface: A continental visitor finds you've been upset, and calls it a flop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns an archaic form of 'you' upside down; in a down clue that reads it from the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: A turkey is slang for a flop, especially a play or film that fails badly.

clue.text: Engineers in, supporting church buttress

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers
to be for something is to support it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Engineers are brought in to shore up a church with a buttress.
explanation.definitionFit: To buttress is to strengthen or prop up, a direct synonym when used as a verb.

clue.text: Opening article penned by doctor

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed within it, so the article goes inside the doctor

parts.note: a GP is a general practitioner
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A doctor writes the opening article of a journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned' looks like writing but means enclosed: A goes inside GP.
explanation.definitionFit: A gap is an opening or space through which one can pass.

clue.text: Inexperienced member of political party

definitions.meaning: a novice can be described as raw or untrained

explanation.surface: A newcomer to party politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means naive or untrained, and a Green is a member of an environmentalist party.

clue.text: Friend coming to cathedral city in half-hearted fashion

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Ely is a cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: A friend reluctantly visits a cathedral city.
explanation.definitionFit: Done palely means done feebly or weakly, without vigour, like a pale imitation.

clue.text: Protester when head of state appears at end of month

indicators.note: the head of state is placed after the month, at its end

parts.note: March is a month
ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen

explanation.surface: A demonstrator turns up when the monarch appears at the end of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the crossword Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A marcher takes part in a protest march, so is a demonstrator.

clue.text: Claim by trader to be perfect

explanation.surface: A merchant boasting that his goods are flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is read as two words, I DEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as a phrase it is a dealer's statement; as one word it means flawless or best possible.

clue.text: A tranquil ref gets rattled in cup match

indicators.note: a rattled thing is shaken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A calm referee loses his cool in a knockout tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets rattled' signals an anagram of A TRANQUIL REF.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarterfinal is a knockout round in a cup competition, played among the last eight.

clue.text: Bad person turning crazy in Dutch city

parts.note: a rotter is a cad or scoundrel

indicators.note: turning means the word for crazy is read backwards

parts.note: mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A scoundrel goes mad somewhere in the Netherlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' reverses MAD to DAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is a major port city in the Netherlands.

clue.text: When Christians celebrate Pentecost a bit

definitions.meaning: a tiny amount, as in 'not one bit'

explanation.surface: Christians mark Pentecost a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Whit is short for Whitsun, the Pentecost season, and a whit is the smallest amount.

clue.text: Bird caged by our headmaster

indicators.note: the bird is held inside the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Our head teacher keeps a bird in a cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caged by' signals the answer is held within ouR HEAdmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhea is a large flightless South American bird related to the ostrich.

clue.text: See hunt going out and sound keen!

indicators.note: the letters going out are scattered and reassembled in another order

explanation.surface: Watch the hunt set off and show your excitement!
explanation.walkthrough: 'going out' signals an anagram of SEE HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To enthuse is to speak eagerly and excitedly about something.

clue.text: Plod randomly round Austria's capital with good person in attendance

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes round the capital letter
letters arranged randomly are in a jumbled order
a capital letter is the first, so take the first of the country

explanation.surface: A plodding policeman wanders round Vienna with a well-behaved companion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'randomly' shuffles PLOD; 'round' puts it around A (first letter of Austria's).
explanation.definitionFit: A lapdog is a servile follower who always stays at someone's side.

clue.text: Right famous detective novelist!

definitions.meaning: on the right-hand side, from the Latin for right

explanation.surface: Quite so, a well-known crime writer!
explanation.walkthrough: Colin Dexter wrote the Inspector Morse novels, set in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Dexter is the heraldic term for the right-hand side, and Colin Dexter is a celebrated crime author.

clue.text: Performances deemed very good? I came seventh, surprisingly

indicators.note: the letters fall out unexpectedly, in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A competitor boasts about finishing seventh, to everyone's surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' signals an anagram of I CAME SEVENTH.
explanation.definitionFit: Achievements are accomplishments, things done well, hence performances regarded highly.

clue.text: Girl in mist going over lake

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece going over the other sits above it

parts.note: haze is a light mist

explanation.surface: A girl lost in fog drifts out over the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' puts HAZE above L in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Hazel is a female given name.

clue.text: Paris's first person on street to make a joke

parts.note: je is French for I, the first person singular

explanation.surface: The first Parisian you meet on the street cracks a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paris's' means in French; 'first person' is the pronoun I, French JE.
explanation.definitionFit: To jest is to speak in fun or tell a quip.

clue.text: Character at end, after party, had a kip

indicators.note: the character comes after the party in the answer

parts.note: a do is a party
zed is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone nods off at the end of the night after a party.
explanation.walkthrough: ZED is the British name for the letter Z.
explanation.definitionFit: A kip is a nap, so to have one is to have slept lightly.

clue.text: Malign notice interrupts attempt to stop war

indicators.note: the notice breaks into the ceasefire, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a truce is a ceasefire
an ad is a notice or advertisement

explanation.surface: A spiteful notice disrupts peace negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Malign' looks like an adjective but is the verb definition; 'attempt to stop war' is a ceasefire, not a peace bid.
explanation.definitionFit: To traduce is to slander or speak ill of someone, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Fool making girl lose her head

indicators.note: the girl loses her head, her first letter is dropped

parts.note: lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A silly girl loses her head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose her head' removes the first letter of LASS.
explanation.definitionFit: An ass is a silly or stupid person.

clue.text: Female prisoner backsliding

indicators.note: sliding back means the word for prisoner is read backwards

parts.note: a lag is a convict, as in 'old lag'

explanation.surface: A woman convict relapses into crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backsliding' reverses LAG, slang for a convict.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is a colloquial word for a girl or woman.

clue.text: Confused state means rest will be disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Muddle means your sleep will be broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be disturbed' signals an anagram of MEANS REST.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a muddle or a complicated, chaotic situation.
